meta.basis: 100 synthetic acquisition, search-intent, and product-identity validation cases rewritten from internet research across inspection negotiation articles, lender concession guidance, state inspection workflows, FHA/VA property standards, and existing inspection-report request-builder products.
meta.warning: These are internet-researched synthetic cases, not verified customer interviews, legal advice, lending advice, or form instructions.

cases.sourceBasis: SERP pattern: inspection response letter searches often need a sendable negotiation packet, not a generic blog explanation.
cases.persona: Buyer agent searching inspection response letter template
cases.deal: Inspection contingency expires tomorrow and buyer wants a concise response to seller.
cases.requiredGate: tool-first packet generation with buyer approval
cases.riskIfWrong: Visitor gets an article when their acquisition intent is immediate document drafting.

cases.sourceBasis: Repair-credit guidance: credit wording and lender visibility can matter as much as the negotiated amount.

cases.deal: Conventional buyer has low cash after closing and wants a credit for urgent repairs.

cases.riskIfWrong: Product promises economic value the buyer may not be able to use at closing.

cases.sourceBasis: Negotiation articles distinguish seller repair work from buyer-controlled post-close credit outcomes.

expectedLeadScope: licensed electrical repair or equivalent credit
cases.riskIfWrong: Buyer accepts low-quality seller work when a credit or licensed completion proof was the real need.

cases.sourceBasis: Seller-refusal guidance: when seller says no, product should narrow to deal-critical items and contingency choices.

cases.sourceBasis: Inspection report builders already support custom text; new product must show domain judgment with lender and negotiation rules.
cases.persona: Agent who already uses Spectora repair builder
cases.deal: Agent can create a list but needs help deciding credit versus repair.
findings: seller is relocating and cannot manage repairs
cases.riskIfWrong: Agent sees no added value over their existing report tool.

cases.sourceBasis: Seller counter offer searches often need a concise comparison matrix for the buyer, not more prose.
cases.persona: Buyer agent preparing counter comparison
cases.deal: Seller offers repairs for some items and credit for others.
cases.riskIfWrong: Buyer cannot see which risks remain after the counter.

cases.sourceBasis: Inspection negotiation content often recommends specialist quotes for high-cost systems.
cases.persona: Buyer agent handling old HVAC negotiation
cases.deal: HVAC is old, working intermittently, and replacement quote is requested.
findings: seller says age was priced in
cases.riskIfWrong: Seller dismisses the ask as replacement due to age rather than malfunction.

cases.sourceBasis: What-not-to-ask acquisition path can be a lead qualifier: some cases should recommend no packet.
cases.persona: Buyer searching should I ask for credit for minor repairs
cases.deal: Inspection is clean and market is competitive.
cases.riskIfWrong: Product generates a pointless request and damages the agent's credibility.

cases.sourceBasis: Tool-first versus article intent: emergency deadline users need immediate triage and cannot consume long educational content.
cases.persona: Agent with inspection deadline tonight
cases.deal: Inspection period expires at midnight and buyer wants a credit request.
cases.riskIfWrong: User misses the inspection-period action window while reading content.

cases.sourceBasis: Product identity should distinguish negotiation packet from home warranty sales or contractor marketplace lead-gen.
cases.persona: Buyer agent wary of contractor lead-gen tools
cases.deal: Agent wants client advice without pushing vendor referrals.
findings: tool asks for buyer phone before output
expectedExclusions: home warranty upsell as primary answer
cases.riskIfWrong: Agents avoid the tool because it feels like lead capture for contractors.

cases.sourceBasis: Searchers asking for inspection response letter may need a productized buyer-agent deliverable for listing agents and clients.
cases.persona: Agent building premium buyer service package
cases.deal: Agent wants inspection negotiation packet as differentiator in buyer consultation.
cases.riskIfWrong: Product only serves live deals and misses acquisition before agent commitment.

cases.sourceBasis: Public seller-credit guidance highlights timing: credits discovered too late can cause lender and closing-document friction.
cases.persona: Closing coordinator handling late seller credit
cases.deal: Buyer and seller agree to a credit at final walkthrough for incomplete repair.
findings: seller did not finish plumbing repair
cases.riskIfWrong: Product suggests a side arrangement or last-minute credit that disrupts closing.

cases.sourceBasis: Acquisition pages should handle no-report searches by offering checklist education, not hallucinated case facts.
cases.persona: Prospective buyer before inspection
cases.deal: Buyer searches what should I ask seller to fix before inspection is complete.
findings: buyer saw old roof during showing
cases.riskIfWrong: Tool fabricates a negotiation packet before evidence exists.

cases.sourceBasis: A strong acquisition case for product-led SEO combines immediate output, scope discipline, lender caveats, and team workflow.
cases.persona: Buyer-agent team lead searching inspection response letter generator
cases.deal: Team wants to standardize live inspection negotiations across several states.
cases.requiredGate: product identity as negotiation workflow, not content or report software
cases.riskIfWrong: The acquisition engine brings qualified teams but the product category feels wrong.
